question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x={sech}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1-\operatorname{tanh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x(1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1-\operatorname{tanh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡(1-\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x(1-\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡x(1-\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x})\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
